hypothesis_statement.content: The paper proposes a gradient-based co-design framework to jointly optimize topology, material distribution, and control policy.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this work, we propose a gradient-based co-design framework that simultaneously optimizes the topology, material distribution, and control policy of a truss-lattice robot.

hypothesis_statement.content: The paper proposes a framework to jointly co-design structure, material layout, and control of a discrete truss-lattice robot.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this work, we propose a framework that co-designs the structure, material layout, and control of a discrete truss-lattice robot (Fig. 1).

hypothesis_statement.content: The method constructs a unified spatial-temporal design space combining structure, material selection, and neural control training.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We begin by constructing a unified spatial-temporal design space, merging structure and material selections with control neural network training (Fig. 1a).

hypothesis_statement.content: The method uses a GPU-enabled differentiable dynamic simulation for performance and sensitivity evaluation.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We then develop a GPU-enabled differentiable dynamic simulation to quantify system performance and sensitivity (Fig. 1b).

hypothesis_statement.content: The method integrates representation and differentiable evaluation into constrained optimization for concurrent updates of all design entities.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We integrate the representation and differentiable evaluation into a constrained optimization to iteratively and concurrently update all design entities (Fig. 1c).

hypothesis_statement.content: A continuous differentiable representation can unify topology, discrete material choice, and spatiotemporal neural control for gradient-based optimization.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We introduce a continuous, differentiable design representation that unifies spatial topological, discrete material selection, and spatiotemporal neural control in a discrete robot, enabling the use of efficient gradient-based optimization.

hypothesis_statement.content: A GPU-parallel differentiable simulator can capture physical interdependence and efficiently evaluate contact-rich dynamics while providing gradients.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We develop a GPU-parallel differentiable simulator that captures the physical interdependency among design entities and their environment, efficiently evaluating dynamics in contact-rich scenarios while providing gradient information through automatic differentiation.

hypothesis_statement.content: A constrained optimization can jointly design structure, materials, and control for automated dynamic robot design.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We propose a constrained optimization method that jointly designs structure, materials, and control to automate dynamic robot design.

hypothesis_statement.content: The framework jointly co-designs topology, material distribution, and temporal control to maximize dynamic performance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Our goal is to co-design the topology, the spatial distribution of material types, and the temporal control signals for each actuator to maximize dynamic performance.

hypothesis_statement.content: The method extends topology optimization with mixed-variable representation, differentiable simulation, and constrained optimization.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To achieve this, we extend topology optimization to integrate a mixed-variable design representation, a differentiable dynamic simulation for design evaluation, and a constrained optimization for design synthesis.

hypothesis_statement.content: An auxiliary stability evaluation with a sharpened proxy geometry is proposed to assess final discrete-robot integrity.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To reliably probe the structural integrity of the final discrete robot, we propose to implement an auxiliary stability evaluation along with the ordinary objective function evaluation.

hypothesis_statement.content: The proposed platform can navigate the mixed-variable space and co-design should improve dynamic performance over separate design.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We first investigate whether the proposed platform can effectively navigate the mixed-variable design space to discover optimal configurations of topology, material layout, and control. Furthermore, we verify whether co-design yields improved dynamic performance by comparing our method against a baseline that designs configuration and control separately

causal_claim.content: GPU-parallel physics solvers accelerate evaluations, and automatic differentiation through the simulation graph enables efficient long-horizon gradient computation even with discontinuous contacts; together these advances enable gradient-based co-design frameworks that require far fewer simulations than exhaustive or heuristic optimization.
evidence_spans: In particular, GPU-parallel physics solvers dramatically accelerate evaluations [34, 35],
while auto-differentiation [36, 37] enables efficient calculation of gradients over long temporal horizons for design variables, even in the presence of discontinuous contacts.

The resulting procedure also defines a forward computational graph, which allows automatic differentiation to backpropagate the sensitivity of the nodal displacement at the final state through all integration time steps to the design variables and weights of control networks. This yields the gradients required to update the design variables and control weights.

These advances have enabled a range of frameworks that achieve co-design using gradient-based optimization, drastically reducing the number of simulations compared with exhaustive or heuristic optimizers [15, 32, 38, 39, 40].

causal_claim.content: The scaled softmax relaxation projects continuous design variables toward normalized material states approximating one-hot encoding, and explicit/global binarization and orthogonality penalties further push intermediate material vectors toward discrete one-hot states.

Second, we impose binarization constraints on the material state vectors to ensure they eventually achieve a fully discretized state, i.e., ˜zij,k ∈{0, 1} (Fig. 4). This is accomplished through a global binarization penalty gbin that drives the L2 norm of the material state vector toward 1 [39], and a pairwise orthogonal penalty gortho that minimizes the overlap between entries corresponding to any two distinct material types:

hypothesis_statement.content: The paper proposes a gradient-based co-design framework for discrete truss-lattice robots that jointly optimizes topology/structure, material distribution/layout, and spatiotemporal/temporal control policy/signals to maximize dynamic performance.
evidence_spans: In this work, we propose a gradient-based co-design framework that simultaneously optimizes the topology, material distribution, and control policy of a truss-lattice robot.
In this work, we propose a framework that co-designs the structure, material layout, and control of a discrete truss-lattice robot (Fig. 1).
Our goal is to co-design the topology, the spatial distribution of material types, and the temporal control signals for each actuator to maximize dynamic performance.

hypothesis_statement.content: The core hypothesis/method claim is that a unified continuous, differentiable mixed-variable spatial-temporal design representation—combining topology/structure, discrete material selection, and neural control—together with GPU-parallel differentiable dynamic simulation and constrained optimization enables concurrent gradient-based updates of all design entities for automated dynamic robot design.
evidence_spans: We begin by constructing a unified spatial-temporal design space, merging structure and material selections with control neural network training (Fig. 1a).
We then develop a GPU-enabled differentiable dynamic simulation to quantify system performance and sensitivity (Fig. 1b).
We integrate the representation and differentiable evaluation into a constrained optimization to iteratively and concurrently update all design entities (Fig. 1c).

We introduce a continuous, differentiable design representation that unifies spatial topological, discrete material selection, and spatiotemporal neural control in a discrete robot, enabling the use of efficient gradient-based optimization.

We develop a GPU-parallel differentiable simulator that captures the physical interdependency among design entities and their environment, efficiently evaluating dynamics in contact-rich scenarios while providing gradient information through automatic differentiation.
We propose a constrained optimization method that jointly designs structure, materials, and control to automate dynamic robot design.

To achieve this, we extend topology optimization to integrate a mixed-variable design representation, a differentiable dynamic simulation for design evaluation, and a constrained optimization for design synthesis.
